skill.name: champion-tracker
skill.description: Checks a list of former buyers and customer advocates against Leadsets data. Reports employer and role changes, work email status, and records that need review.
skill.summary: Track employer changes among former buyers and customer advocates.
skill.author: leadsets

security_audit.summary: No evidence was found of shell execution, environment access, system reconnaissance, or prompt injection. The workflow sends contact identifiers to Leadsets but does not require explicit approval for that transfer. It also lacks a per-contact identity check before reporting new work emails.

remediation.issue: Approval does not explicitly cover third-party processing of contact data.
remediation.suggestion: Show the Leadsets destination and exact fields to be sent, and obtain approval before enrichment. Send only the identifiers needed for matching.

remediation.issue: A verified work email does not confirm that the enrichment result belongs to the intended contact.
remediation.suggestion: Require a reliable identity match for each contact before exporting their email or recording a move. Send ambiguous matches to manual review.

content.user_title: Track Job Changes for Past Customer Champions
content.value_statement: Contact lists can fall out of date when former buyers change jobs. Compare your list with Leadsets data to identify employer moves, role changes, and work email verification status.
actual_capabilities: Reads an accessible CSV, Google Sheet, or CRM view and removes duplicate contacts.
Checks Leadsets usage limits, tests one contact, and groups the remaining lookups into batches.
Compares current and prior employer domains and titles to distinguish company moves from role changes.
Separates verified, catch-all, unknown, and missing work emails in the report.
Exports results to CSV or a connected Google Sheet or CRM, and reports skipped rows and pending batches.
limitations: Requires a Leadsets account and a configured MCP connection or REST API key.
Processes the list on request and does not establish the actual date a contact started a new job.
Does not guarantee a match or a verified work email for every contact.
Does not send outreach, create sequences, or find replacements at a contact's former company.

use_cases.title: Review an old buyer list
use_cases.description: Find former buyers at new employers before you prepare your own follow-up.

use_cases.title: Track changes across CRM exports
use_cases.description: Compare a monthly export with the previous report and separate employer moves from internal role changes.

use_cases.title: Check where early customers work now
use_cases.description: Review a short list of former customer advocates and flag cases that need manual checking.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner: Review a CSV
prompt_templates.scenario: Check a short list of former buyers.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my attached CSV for employer changes. Before enrichment, show me what will be sent to Leadsets and wait for my approval. Return the results as a CSV.

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: Separate moves from role changes
prompt_templates.scenario: Review a list that includes prior employers and titles.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the company domains and titles in this sheet as the baseline. Separate employer moves from role changes, and flag possible rebrands for review. Return verified work emails only.

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: Compare with a previous report
prompt_templates.scenario: Repeat a monthly review with a 60-day follow-up window.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use last month's report as the baseline for the matched contacts in this export. Set follow-up dates 60 days after detection. Do not treat detection dates as job start dates.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: Run a large review within quota
prompt_templates.scenario: Review a CRM contact list without exceeding remaining enrichment records.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check the remaining Leadsets quota and propose a batch plan. Wait for approval before enrichment and flag uncertain identities for review. Return a CSV, with no CRM writes, and list any pending batches.

output_examples.input: Check 25 unique contacts from this approved export and report employer changes.
output: Checked 25 contacts: 4 employer moves, 3 role changes, 16 unchanged, 1 not found, and 1 needs review.
Among the 4 moves, 2 work emails were verified, 1 was catch-all, and 1 was missing.

output_examples.input: Check this approved list of 80 contacts and pause at the current enrichment limit.
output: Checked 50 contacts and found 7 employer moves.
The remaining 30 contacts were not checked. Resume when the Leadsets usage window resets.

best_practices: Use stable identifiers such as LinkedIn URLs where available, and review uncertain matches before using returned addresses.
Confirm which identifiers may be sent to Leadsets and who can access the output before running enrichment.
Reuse the last confirmed report as the baseline when tracking changes over time.
anti_patterns: Treating a catch-all or unknown work email as verified.
Assuming the date a move was detected is the contact's start date.
Treating every domain change as a new employer without considering rebrands or parent companies.

faq.question: What does each input row need?
faq.answer: Provide a full name and the last known company or domain. A LinkedIn URL improves matching.

faq.question: Do I need a Leadsets account?
faq.answer: Yes. Connect Leadsets through MCP or configure access with a REST API key.

faq.question: How many records does a check use?
faq.answer: A lookup that returns data uses one enrichment record. A not-found lookup still uses a request but does not use an enrichment record.

faq.question: Does verified mean the contact is the right person?
faq.answer: No. Verification describes the email status returned by Leadsets. Check the person's identity separately when a match is uncertain.

faq.question: What does the default 90-day window measure?
faq.answer: It starts on the date the move is first detected, not on the person's first day at the new company.

faq.question: Will it send emails or overwrite CRM fields?
faq.answer: It does not send emails. A selected CRM destination uses notes or tasks unless you ask to update fields.
